title: Game 12: Capablanca–Chajes
subtitle: The king becomes an attacking piece while queens remain

narration.say: Capablanca has White against Chajes at New York in 1918. White develops the bishop to d3.
White recaptures and exchanges knights on f6.
Black castles. White pins the knight, then exchanges it.
Black has advanced g6. White can begin a pawn demonstration on the h-file.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Start the kingside pawn advance.

steps.title: A pawn gain and an active rook

narration.say: White captures e5. Black develops the bishop with tempo, and White retreats the queen.
White castles queenside and recaptures the bishop with the rook.
Both sides develop their remaining rooks.

steps.title: Fix the queenside before changing wings

narration.say: Black advances c5. White activates the king and gains queenside space.
The queens manoeuvre while White keeps the rook active.

steps.title: A protected route for the king

narration.say: White supports the queenside and begins king manoeuvres.
White advances g4, while the queens continue manoeuvring.
The king travels to g3. It will protect squares the black queen might use for counterplay.

steps.title: Open the kingside with king support

narration.say: The king is now ready to support the attack. White advances the h-pawn.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Break open the kingside pawn formation.

steps.title: A rook on the seventh rank

narration.say: White recaptures with the g-pawn. The queen comes to f5.
White’s rook can invade the seventh rank.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Bring the rook to d7.

steps.title: The king remains an active fighter

narration.say: White answers the check by advancing the king. The knight captures the bishop.
Black resigns. White’s king has become an attacking piece even though the queens are still on the board.

steps.title: King activity is a concrete decision

narration.say: White first fixed the queenside and secured the squares needed for the king’s route.
The king’s arrival supported the pawn break and the rook invasion.
This is not permission to expose your king carelessly. The route was prepared and the opponent’s counterplay had to be considered.
